title: Learner 01 | Day 001: Files, folders, and the interpreter
body:
## What you will build

Add the **project name** to LearnForge’s first screen. Start by running the [small example and its line-by-line explanation](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/LearnForge/blob/main/days/day-001.md).

## Open this file

`src/learnforge/experience/onboarding/learner_01.py`

The file already contains:

```python
def project_title():
    project_name = "Pending"
    return project_name
```

Change `project_name` from `"Pending"` to **`"LearnForge"`**. Keep the four spaces before the two body lines.

**Input:** `project_title()` receives nothing. **Expected return:** the text `"LearnForge"`. The runner will display that value; this function does not print it.

## Run and check

Run `python run_first_steps.py`. Your part of the screen must show:

```text
Project: LearnForge
```

Change only your local value. Other learners own the other screen lines.

## Hints to research

1. Search `Python variable assignment string number` in [the Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/).
2. Search `Python def indentation return versus print`. Read one small example with the coach.
3. Temporarily change the value again. Predict the displayed line, run, explain the difference, then restore `"LearnForge"`.

## Finish

Show the normal and changed-value run. With @YogeshPatil991, explain what each line does, which name/value changes, and how the returned value reaches the screen.

**Question of the Day:** When does this function’s body run? What does `return` do here?

[Full first lesson](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/LearnForge/blob/main/days/day-001.md) · [Your walkthrough](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/LearnForge/blob/main/lessons/learner-01/day-001.md) · [Execution picture](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/LearnForge/blob/main/EXECUTION_VISUALS.md)
architecture_topic: Separate stored instructions from a running process. A stopped process cannot remember yesterday's variables.
placement_reason: A small welcome-screen value producer; the provided runner owns printing.
